pages.title: Prompt Quality Standards
pages.excerpt: Understand how Samith AI evaluates prompt clarity, usefulness, originality, responsible use, and real-world test evidence before publication.
pages.seo_title: Prompt Quality Standards | Samith AI Creator Guide
pages.meta_description: Learn the standards behind clear, reusable and responsible AI prompts, including testing, revisions, evidence and moderation.
pages.body_html:
High-quality prompts are designed to be useful, understandable, and testable. Samith AI encourages creators to describe a real task, provide a clear method, and make the limitations of AI output visible. Our quality standards help guide creation and editorial review; they are not a claim that every available prompt has been independently certified or will produce identical results.

1. Clear purpose and intended audience

Every product should explain what problem it helps solve, who is likely to benefit, and what a successful output looks like. Titles should be specific and accurate. Summaries should communicate the use case without inflated claims, unsupported superlatives, or fabricated results. A product that covers several distinct workflows should clearly separate them.

2. Complete, reusable instructions

A strong prompt ordinarily includes a role or context, a clear objective, labeled input variables, an ordered process, expected output headings, and relevant restrictions. The user should know which information to provide, which details are optional, and how to adapt the instructions for another scenario.

  • Use meaningful placeholders such as [AUDIENCE], [GOAL], [SOURCE FACTS], or [OUTPUT FORMAT].
  • Specify requested structure, length, tone, language, audience, and measurable constraints.
  • Distinguish user-provided facts from assumptions the model may need to make.
  • Provide a practical self-check, revision instruction, or acceptance criterion where appropriate.

Instructions should be readable, free of unnecessary complexity, and reasonably portable when no specific model feature is required.

3. Real-world usefulness

The product should address a recognizable task and save the user unnecessary trial and error. We evaluate whether its intended output would be actionable, understandable, and proportionate to the request. Good examples demonstrate the workflow without replacing a user's judgment or making claims about guaranteed productivity gains.

4. Accuracy, honesty, and evidence

Creators must not invent research findings, testimonials, rankings, customer results, licenses, credentials, reviews, or test statistics. Prompts that ask an AI tool to use outside information should make verification requirements explicit. If source material is not supplied, the prompt should ask for it or mark uncertain claims for checking.

For educational, technical, analytical, financial, legal, or health-related tasks, the product should explain why expert review or additional verification may be necessary. AI output is not a substitute for reliable primary sources, authorized testing, or qualified professional advice.

5. Originality and intellectual-property responsibility

Product descriptions and prompts must be original or used with appropriate permission. Do not copy another seller's restricted listing, redistribute proprietary training material, or include unlicensed assets. Creators should avoid asking users to violate intellectual-property rights and should disclose relevant source or attribution requirements where applicable.

6. Safety, privacy, and fairness

Prompts should not request passwords, secret API keys, unnecessary personal information, or confidential customer records. Where real data is needed, explain anonymization, consent, and secure handling. Instructions should avoid discriminatory assumptions, manipulative claims, deceptive impersonation, or harmful conduct.

Quality includes accessibility: plain-language instructions, readable formatting, meaningful alternatives when possible, and appropriate cultural and linguistic review.

7. Compatibility and limitations

Identify the task type—such as text generation, coding, image design, or video planning—and any tool-specific features genuinely required. A prompt should not claim universal compatibility or guaranteed results across AI models. When creators name a provider or model, they should document the version actually tested and review the listing as provider features change.

See AI Tools & Compatibility for practical selection and testing guidance.

8. Evidence-based testing

Where feasible, creators should run the completed prompt with a sanitized, realistic example and an independent second input. A useful test record identifies the AI provider or model, model version if available, test scenario, date, observed behavior, factual or technical problems, and changes made after review. Do not state that a prompt was tested if it was not.

Samith AI includes a private Prompt Quality Center for designated starter products. Its records are entered by human reviewers; the platform does not automatically execute an AI model when a result is saved. For that starter collection, a current administrator-recorded passing review and required quality checks are prerequisites for submission. Changing substantive content invalidates that previous pass and requires another review.

9. Review outcomes and improvements

A prompt may remain a draft, need revision, enter a submission queue, or be approved for publication according to the applicable workflow. A quality note documents a particular review at a particular time. It is not an endorsement by an AI provider, a legal guarantee, or a promise of future performance.

Creators should update listings when prompts become misleading, rely on obsolete tool features, or require additional guidance. Users who discover a problem can contact the Support Center with enough non-confidential detail to help investigate.

Creator pre-submission checklist

  1. Confirm that the title and description accurately match the actual prompt.
  2. Complete every reusable variable, process step, and output requirement.
  3. Run realistic tests where possible and record honest evidence.
  4. Verify sources, claims, calculations, code, and generated assets as appropriate.
  5. Check originality, privacy, safety, accessibility, and cultural fit.
  6. Disclose model-specific dependencies, limitations, and rights restrictions.
  7. Review the final version again before choosing Submit.

Review Become a Creator for the submission workflow and Responsible AI Usage for more detail on handling AI results.

pages.title: AI Tools & Compatibility
pages.excerpt: Find out how to choose an AI tool for text, coding, images, video, and research workflows, and how to test prompt compatibility responsibly.
pages.seo_title: AI Tools and Compatibility Guide | Samith AI
pages.meta_description: Learn which AI tool capabilities matter for Samith AI prompts and how to test model fit, availability, outputs, and limitations.
pages.body_html:
A useful prompt starts with the right kind of AI tool. Samith AI offers instructions for different tasks, from business writing and lesson planning to software development and creative production. Not every prompt is suitable for every model. Compatibility depends on the provider, available features, model version, user account, plan, input limits, and the task itself.

Samith AI is an independent prompt marketplace. References to third-party AI tools are descriptive examples, not claims of official partnership, endorsement, or guaranteed integration. Provider capabilities and terms can change.

Choose the tool by the task

Text and conversation workflows

Use a text-capable assistant for drafting, planning, editing, summarization, research question development, and structured written outputs. Examples of third-party text assistants include ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, subject to the features available in your account and location. Check that the tool can process your prompt length and produce the desired language and format.

Programming and software workflows

Code-focused assistants and developer tools can help with specifications, code explanations, testing ideas, and review checklists. A generated patch is not automatically safe, buildable, or production-ready. Verify APIs and framework versions, inspect dependencies, run automated tests, review security and permissions, and use a staging environment before deployment.

Image-generation workflows

Image prompts work with tools that support the requested visual generation or editing operation. Consider the input format (text-only versus reference image), aspect ratio, resolution, typography handling, permitted content, consistency controls, and commercial-use conditions. A prompt written as art direction for an image tool will not produce an image in a text-only assistant.

Video and motion workflows

Some products are creative briefs or shot lists for video workflows, while others may require a video-generation provider. Check whether your chosen service supports text-to-video, image-to-video, shot duration, aspect ratio, audio, and asset upload. Motion and character continuity should be checked shot by shot. Do not assume any particular generation feature is available without confirming it in the provider interface.

Research and data workflows

Planning and analysis prompts may help explain a method, design a survey, or draft code for a statistical tool. They do not replace your dataset, calculations, source verification, or methodological review. A model that cannot access your actual sources should not be asked to invent citations or statistical results.

What to check before using a prompt

  • Required modality: Does the task need text, code, a file, an image, video, or a combination?
  • Inputs: Can the AI tool accept the data type, size, language, and context required?
  • Outputs: Can it produce the requested structure, file format, aspect ratio, or code language?
  • Model/version: Is the feature still available on the provider and plan you use?
  • Privacy and rights: Are you permitted to upload the data, source materials, and media assets?
  • Tool settings: Do system instructions, temperature, plugins, integrations, or account limits materially affect the result?

A five-step compatibility test

  1. Read the product: identify the task type, required inputs, tool assumptions, and output.
  2. Try a safe example: use fictional or anonymized data rather than real secrets or sensitive records.
  3. Check the format: confirm that all requested sections, variables, and constraints appear.
  4. Check the substance: independently verify factual claims, calculations, links, generated code, or media details.
  5. Record what changed: note the tool and version used, limitations, and any edits to the prompt.

Why the same prompt can give different results

AI tools may use different model architectures, training data, tool access, safety policies, output settings, and context windows. A single provider may also change features or retire a model. The language of a prompt can be interpreted differently across runs. For this reason, a test on one model should not be described as proof that the prompt will perform identically everywhere.

Language and localization

Samith AI supports a multilingual website experience, but the presence of a language option does not mean that every product has a reviewed translation. For Khmer, English, or another language, ask for the desired register, terminology, and target audience. Have a knowledgeable human review important translations and culturally sensitive information before use.

Independent providers and costs

A Samith AI prompt product does not necessarily include access to an external AI provider, a paid subscription, API credits, generated media, or separate tool licenses. You are responsible for checking the provider's terms, pricing, availability, and account requirements. Only use tools and features you are authorized to access.

Frequently asked questions

Does buying or accessing a prompt include an AI subscription?

No automatic inclusion should be assumed. Check the product's listing and the AI provider's current requirements separately.

Can I use an image prompt in a chat assistant?

Only if the particular assistant supports image generation or an appropriate connected image tool. Otherwise it may help revise the wording, but it cannot supply the requested image output.

Can a prompt be moved between models?

Often its underlying method can be adapted, but constraints and results may change. Retest and update instructions for the new environment.

How do I report compatibility issues?

Use the Support Center. Include the product name, model/version if known, expected result, and a sanitized description of what occurred.

For guidance on reviewing results, read Prompt Quality Standards and Responsible AI Usage.

Review third-party model examples and links periodically as tools change

pages.title: Responsible AI Usage
pages.excerpt: Practical guidance for protecting privacy, checking accuracy, respecting intellectual property, and making informed decisions when using AI-generated content.
pages.seo_title: Responsible AI Usage | Privacy, Accuracy and Human Review
pages.meta_description: Use AI prompts responsibly: protect sensitive information, verify outputs, respect rights, address bias, and keep a human in control.
pages.body_html:
Artificial intelligence can help people explore ideas, organize information, create drafts, and solve practical problems. It can also make mistakes with remarkable confidence. Responsible AI use means staying informed, protecting people and information, and keeping humans accountable for decisions. This guide is educational guidance for Samith AI users and creators. It supplements—but does not replace—the platform's applicable policies and the terms of any third-party AI provider.

1. Keep a human accountable

Use AI output as a starting point, not automatic proof that something is correct, appropriate, legal, or ready to publish. A person who understands the task should review important facts and make the final decision. Organizations should assign clear responsibility for approvals, corrections, and any impact on customers or employees.

2. Protect privacy and confidential information

Do not enter passwords, API keys, payment card information, private account records, sensitive medical data, unpublished business plans, or personal customer information into an AI tool without appropriate authority and a clear understanding of the provider's data controls. When possible, replace real names, email addresses, identifiers, and confidential figures with fictional or anonymized examples.

Check whether your organization permits the tool, how data is retained, who can access the inputs and outputs, and whether your usage requires consent or additional safeguards. A prompt that asks for personal data should request only what is truly necessary for the task.

3. Verify accuracy and sources

AI-generated answers can contain invented citations, incorrect dates, faulty calculations, nonexistent features, and misleading summaries. For consequential work, compare claims with reliable sources, original documents, validated datasets, or qualified experts. Ask the model to distinguish documented evidence from assumptions; then verify the evidence yourself.

  • Check names, dates, quotations, URLs, numbers, and statistical conclusions.
  • Do not present made-up citations, reviews, testimonials, or case studies as real.
  • For software, inspect code, dependencies, security, test results, and deployment conditions.
  • For images and video, check visual accuracy, consent, and whether output could mislead viewers.

4. Respect originality and intellectual property

Use source text, images, recordings, data, and brand assets only when you have permission or a valid legal basis to do so. Do not copy another creator's restricted prompt product, distribute protected source materials, or ask AI tools to imitate an identifiable person's work in a way that infringes their rights. Check the specific rights attached to generated content and the third-party tool's rules before using it commercially.

Keep records of assets, licenses, and permissions where appropriate. Samith AI product access does not automatically grant rights to redistribute the prompt itself, resell it, or claim exclusive ownership of a third-party creation. Review the actual published policies and the relevant product license.

5. Reduce bias and unfair treatment

AI may reproduce stereotypes, omit perspectives, or make uneven assumptions about language, age, gender, culture, disability, or other personal characteristics. Evaluate examples and recommendations for fairness, dignity, and local context. Avoid using unverified AI in ways that determine a person's access to employment, education, credit, housing, or essential services.

When teaching, hiring, evaluating, or communicating about people, apply clear human review, explainable criteria, and applicable privacy and nondiscrimination requirements.

6. Be transparent about AI assistance

Do not claim that content, research, testimonials, qualifications, or professional decisions are entirely human-created when doing so would mislead others. Disclose meaningful AI involvement when an employer, client, school, law, or platform rule requires it. Never impersonate real individuals or organizations, fabricate endorsements, or create deceptive evidence.

7. Apply extra care in high-impact areas

For medical, legal, financial, safety, mental-health, and other high-stakes situations, use AI as a supplementary information tool, not a substitute for qualified, context-aware professional advice. Do not base emergency decisions, diagnoses, investments, legal filings, or safety-critical controls solely on unverified model output.

For academic work, follow institutional rules on permitted AI support, independent research, plagiarism, citations, and student data. For cybersecurity or system administration, test only systems you own or are authorized to assess, and review potential effects before making changes.

8. Know when not to use AI

Do not automate a workflow when you cannot inspect the outcome, explain the decision, obtain valid consent, or correct a serious error. Avoid uploading protected information to a tool whose retention and access settings you do not understand. If the result could harm someone and there is no practical review process, use a qualified person or a more appropriate method.

9. Use a simple review process

  1. Define: state the real task, intended audience, acceptable outputs, and limits.
  2. Minimize: remove unnecessary sensitive or confidential input data.
  3. Generate: choose an authorized AI service suited to the task and follow its current rules.
  4. Verify: check claims, sources, fairness, security, rights, and suitability.
  5. Decide: obtain human or professional approval when needed.
  6. Document: record material assumptions, model/version where relevant, corrections, and final responsibility.

10. Responsibilities for Samith AI creators

Creators should write original, clear descriptions and test instructions with privacy-safe examples. Never advertise guaranteed performance, invent model tests, or hide major dependencies. When a prompt changes, update descriptions and retest as appropriate. Follow the platform's quality requirements, moderation decisions, content policies, and licensing rules.

Report a concern

If you encounter a misleading product description, unsafe instructions, suspected rights infringement, privacy issue, or significant factual problem, contact the Support Center. Share the product title and a concise explanation, but avoid attaching passwords or other sensitive details. Reports should be reviewed on their merits; reporting does not guarantee a particular result or response time.

Continue learning

Read How It Works for a practical prompt workflow, Prompt Quality Standards for creator review criteria, and AI Tools & Compatibility for choosing a suitable provider.

The principle is simple: protect people, verify important results, respect others' rights, and remain accountable for what you choose to do with AI.
